rv.q: Yet it is also an intelligent, well-played and ultimately potent drama.

But neither character changes or learns anything new. Much of their dialogue consists of previous actions, statistics, headlines, and talking points. You can almost hear Schenkkan saying to himself, “Better put in some personal stuff, so they don’t sound too much like talking heads.”

cn.t: Schenkkan's anti-Trump dystopian two-hander divides critics: some find it a chilling rallying cry for resistance, while others dismiss it as rushed and derivative, though strong performances add dimension.
